text: Wikipedia shows you one page. Today's. But this number has not always been this number.
This is Palimpsest. Eight hundred sixty-two thousand versions of Wikipedia, in MariaDB, questioned through Gemini.
Ask anything, and pick a date. Gemini answers from the paragraphs that stood that day, next to today's answer. Every sentence cites its passage, and every number is checked.

Paste a claim, or drop a screenshot. Palimpsest follows it through every rewording. Twenty-two thousand eight hundred, in 2003. Twenty-six thousand six hundred, in 2006. And today's number, first written on August twenty-second, 2009.
It shows who changed what. This paragraph was deleted at 6:43 in the evening. Two minutes later, it was back.
Even facts move. Who was president on March first, 1925? It depends which year's Wikipedia you ask.
Underneath, every paragraph is a system-versioned row. Vector search and time travel run in one SQL statement.
Any date. Any claim. Every edit. If Wikipedia ever said it, Palimpsest can find it, date it, and answer from it.
